updateTarget.displayName: Amazon SNS: Create, Subscribe, and Publish

tasks.goal: Create the message-distribution channel named sns-beginner-lab-topic in eu-west-2.
tasks.title: Create a standard SNS topic

cliSteps.warning: Run this as a standalone command. Do not include sensitive information in the topic name.

commands.explanation: Creates the fixed-name standard SNS topic. Save the TopicArn returned by this command because later commands require it.
commands.expectedOutput: The output contains TopicArn for sns-beginner-lab-topic in eu-west-2.

cliSteps.explanation: Creates the fixed-name standard SNS topic. Save the TopicArn returned by this command because later commands require it.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The output contains TopicArn for sns-beginner-lab-topic in eu-west-2.

consoleSteps.title: Open the SNS console
consoleSteps.warning: Do not place personal, confidential, or sensitive information in a topic name.
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Amazon SNS console is open for the intended regional lab.

consoleSteps.title: Open topics
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Topics page opens.

consoleSteps.title: Start topic creation
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Create topic page opens.

consoleSteps.title: Select the topic type
consoleSteps.warning: Do not select FIFO for this introductory lab.
consoleSteps.expectedResult: Standard is selected as the topic type.

consoleSteps.title: Name the topic
consoleSteps.warning: Topic type and name cannot be changed after creation.
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The topic name is populated with the fixed lab name.

consoleSteps.title: Create the topic
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The topic Details page displays the topic name and ARN.

consoleSteps.title: Record the topic ARN
consoleSteps.warning: Use this ARN only as an earlier-command output dependency in later steps.
consoleSteps.expectedResult: You have the ARN needed by later CLI commands.

verification.title: Confirm that the topic exists
verification.instruction: In the Console, open the topic Details page and confirm that sns-beginner-lab-topic has an ARN; or use the CLI command below.
verification.expectedResult: The topic properties are returned for the topic ARN from this task.

tasks.whyItMatters: An SNS topic is the logical access point that groups endpoints and receives messages for distribution.

tasks.goal: Attach the harmless fixed sample endpoint sns-lab@example.com to the lab topic.
tasks.title: Create an email subscription

cliSteps.command: aws sns subscribe --topic-arn "<TopicArn from Task 1>" --protocol email --notification-endpoint sns-lab@example.com --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.warning: The sample endpoint is intentionally non-confidential and is not expected to confirm the subscription.

commands.text: aws sns subscribe --topic-arn "<TopicArn from Task 1>" --protocol email --notification-endpoint sns-lab@example.com --region eu-west-2
commands.explanation: Creates an email subscription for the topic ARN returned by Task 1. Replace only the TopicArn placeholder with that earlier command output.
commands.expectedOutput: The output returns SubscriptionArn with the value pending confirmation.

cliSteps.explanation: Creates an email subscription for the topic ARN returned by Task 1. Replace only the TopicArn placeholder with that earlier command output.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The output returns SubscriptionArn with the value pending confirmation.

consoleSteps.title: Open subscriptions
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Subscriptions page opens.

consoleSteps.title: Start subscription creation
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Create subscription page opens.

consoleSteps.title: Select the lab topic
consoleSteps.warning: Select only the topic created in Task 1.
consoleSteps.instruction: Choose the sns-beginner-lab-topic ARN for Topic ARN.

instructions.text: Choose the sns-beginner-lab-topic ARN for Topic ARN.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The lab topic ARN is selected.

consoleSteps.title: Select the protocol
consoleSteps.expectedResult: Email is selected as the endpoint type.

consoleSteps.title: Enter the sample endpoint
consoleSteps.warning: This sample address is not expected to be monitored, so do not expect a confirmation or delivered notification.
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The fixed non-confidential sample endpoint is populated.

consoleSteps.title: Create the subscription
consoleSteps.warning: Email subscriptions require confirmation before they can receive messages.
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The subscription Details page opens.

verification.title: Confirm the pending subscription state
verification.instruction: Run the standalone CLI verification command below using the TopicArn from Task 1.
verification.expectedResult: The returned topic attributes show the subscription state counts; the sample email subscription remains unconfirmed unless its recipient confirms it.

tasks.whyItMatters: Subscriptions connect SNS topics to endpoints that can receive messages. Email subscriptions require confirmation before they can receive published notifications.

tasks.goal: Publish the message SNS beginner lab test message to the standard topic.
tasks.title: Publish a harmless test notification

cliSteps.command: aws sns publish --topic-arn "<TopicArn from Task 1>" --message "SNS beginner lab test message" --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.warning: A MessageId confirms publication acceptance; the pending sample email subscription cannot receive the message until confirmed.

commands.text: aws sns publish --topic-arn "<TopicArn from Task 1>" --message "SNS beginner lab test message" --region eu-west-2
commands.explanation: Publishes the harmless fixed test message to the TopicArn returned by Task 1. Replace only the TopicArn placeholder with that earlier command output.
commands.expectedOutput: The output contains a MessageId, showing that Amazon SNS accepted the publish request.

cliSteps.explanation: Publishes the harmless fixed test message to the TopicArn returned by Task 1. Replace only the TopicArn placeholder with that earlier command output.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The output contains a MessageId, showing that Amazon SNS accepted the publish request.

consoleSteps.title: Open topics
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Topics page opens.

consoleSteps.title: Select the lab topic
consoleSteps.warning: Select only the topic created in Task 1.
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The lab topic is selected.

consoleSteps.title: Open message publishing
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Publish message to topic page opens.

consoleSteps.title: Set the subject
consoleSteps.instruction: Enter SNS beginner lab in Subject.

instructions.text: Enter SNS beginner lab in Subject.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The optional subject is populated.

consoleSteps.title: Choose a shared payload
consoleSteps.instruction: Choose Identical payload for all delivery protocols.

instructions.text: Choose Identical payload for all delivery protocols.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The message editor accepts one payload for all protocols.

consoleSteps.title: Enter the message
consoleSteps.warning: Do not enter confidential information in a notification message.
consoleSteps.instruction: Enter SNS beginner lab test message.

instructions.text: Enter SNS beginner lab test message.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The harmless sample message is populated.

consoleSteps.title: Publish the message
consoleSteps.warning: The sample email subscription is pending confirmation, so delivery to it is not expected.
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The message is published and the topic Details page opens.

verification.title: Confirm that SNS accepted the message
verification.instruction: Confirm that the publish action returned a MessageId in the CLI, or that the Console returned to the topic Details page after publishing.
verification.expectedResult: SNS accepted the test message for the lab topic.

tasks.whyItMatters: Publishing sends a message to the topic, and Amazon SNS attempts delivery to each subscribed endpoint.

phases.title: Create the notification channel
phases.description: Create one standard SNS topic in Europe (London).

phases.title: Add an endpoint and publish a test message
phases.description: Create an email subscription and send a harmless sample notification.

phases.title: Verify and remove the lab resources
phases.description: Confirm the topic behavior, then manually delete only the topic created for this lab.

steps.title: Console cleanup — delete only the lab topic
steps.description: In Amazon SNS for eu-west-2, select only sns-beginner-lab-topic, choose Delete, enter delete me, and choose Delete.
steps.instruction: In Amazon SNS for eu-west-2, select only sns-beginner-lab-topic, choose Delete, enter delete me, and choose Delete.
steps.verification: The topic no longer appears on the Topics page. Its associated sample subscription is deleted asynchronously with the topic.

steps.title: CLI cleanup — delete only the lab topic
steps.description: aws sns delete-topic --topic-arn "<TopicArn from Task 1>" --region eu-west-2
steps.instruction: aws sns delete-topic --topic-arn "<TopicArn from Task 1>" --region eu-west-2
steps.verification: The command produces no output. Use this as an alternative to the Console cleanup route, not in addition to it.

steps.title: CLI cleanup verification
steps.verification: The returned topic ARN list does not include sns-beginner-lab-topic.

warnings.cost: This lab creates one SNS topic, one email subscription request, and one published message. Review applicable Amazon SNS pricing for the account before running the lab.
warnings.region: Use Europe (London), eu-west-2, throughout. Every regional AWS CLI command in this follow along includes --region eu-west-2.
warnings.safety: Use only the fixed harmless topic name and sample message. Do not place personal, confidential, or sensitive information in topic names or notification messages.
warnings.credentials: Do not paste, display, or share credentials. The Console and AWS CLI must already be authorized to perform the documented SNS actions.

programme.subtitle: A beginner lab for learning the basic Amazon Simple Notification Service lifecycle
programme.description: Create a standard Amazon SNS topic, add an email subscription, publish a test notification, and manually remove the lab resources.
programme.displayName: Amazon SNS: Create, Subscribe, and Publish
programme.learningOutcome: Understand how an Amazon SNS topic, subscription, subscription confirmation, and published message fit together in a simple notification workflow.

inputs.buildOutcome: Create and add a complete set of Amazon SNS hands-on labs for the existing Study Tracker app, focused specifically on the AWS Certified Solutions Architect Associate SAA-C03 exam. The app and lab structure already exist, so follow the existing structure, formatting, fields, naming conventions and implementation pattern exactly. Do not describe this as a catalogue, future work, placeholder content, deferred instructions, or something that will be completed later. Every lab must be fully populated and usable. Every lab must be beginner friendly and assume the learner may never have used Amazon SNS before. Every lab must contain BOTH complete AWS Management Console steps and complete AWS CLI steps. Never leave Console actions, CLI actions, validation steps, IAM requirements, explanations or cleanup sections empty. Walk the learner through every important click, field, setting and command, explain what each important option does and why it matters, include expected results and verification steps, and keep programming to an absolute minimum. The first lab must create the IAM user and permissions required for the SNS training labs, including creating the user, explaining why the root account should not be used, assigning suitable permissions using least privilege where practical, signing in as the IAM user, configuring AWS CLI credentials, selecting the AWS Region, testing CLI access and verifying SNS permissions through both the Console and CLI. If later labs use SQS, Lambda, CloudWatch, EventBridge, S3, KMS, HTTP or HTTPS endpoints, email subscriptions, SMS or other AWS services, include and explain the required IAM permissions as part of the relevant lab. Create all practical SNS labs useful for SAA-C03 preparation, including creating Standard SNS topics, understanding topic names and ARNs, publishing messages through Console and CLI, creating and confirming email subscriptions, viewing subscription status, unsubscribing endpoints, deleting subscriptions and topics, SNS to SQS integration, queue policies allowing SNS to send messages, one SNS topic sending to multiple SQS queues, fan-out architectures, multiple subscription types, message attributes, subscription filter policies, filter policy scope, raw message delivery, Standard topic behaviour, at-least-once delivery concepts, SNS FIFO topics, .fifo naming, MessageGroupId, MessageDeduplicationId, content-based deduplication, ordered fan-out to SQS FIFO queues, Standard versus FIFO topics, SNS to Lambda, Lambda execution roles, Lambda subscriptions, granting SNS permission to invoke Lambda, CloudWatch Logs, Lambda failures and retries, SNS direct to Lambda versus SNS to SQS to Lambda, SNS delivery retries, SNS subscription dead-letter queues, failed delivery handling, HTTP and HTTPS subscriptions where safe and practical, EventBridge versus SNS, SNS versus SQS, SNS versus Kinesis, SNS plus SQS fan-out, CloudWatch SNS monitoring, NumberOfMessagesPublished, NumberOfNotificationsDelivered, NumberOfNotificationsFailed, NumberOfNotificationsFilteredOut, CloudWatch alarms, SNS delivery status logging where supported, SNS topic access policies, IAM identity policies versus SNS resource policies, restricting publishers and subscribers, allowing AWS services to publish to SNS, server-side encryption, AWS KMS managed keys, customer managed KMS keys, KMS permissions, encryption at rest, encryption in transit, KMS troubleshooting, cross-account SNS publishing and subscriptions where practical, SMS concepts and optional low-risk SMS labs with clear cost warnings, message size limits, storing oversized payloads in S3 and sending object references, unconfirmed subscriptions, incorrect queue policies, incorrect topic ARNs, incorrect filter policies, missing IAM permissions, KMS failures, Lambda invocation permission failures and delivery troubleshooting. Include practical SAA-C03 architecture scenarios such as one order event reaching billing, inventory and notifications, fan-out without tightly coupling consumers, SNS plus SQS protecting downstream services during traffic spikes, subscribers receiving only relevant message types through filtering, Lambda receiving SNS events directly, durable independent processing through SNS plus SQS, strict ordering using SNS FIFO plus SQS FIFO where appropriate, encrypted pub-sub messaging, cross-account messaging and failed deliveries requiring monitoring or DLQs. Include practical comparison labs for SNS versus SQS, SNS versus EventBridge, SNS versus Kinesis, SNS direct to Lambda versus SNS to SQS to Lambda, Standard SNS versus FIFO SNS, direct application calls versus SNS fan-out and SNS filtering versus sending every message to every subscriber. Every lab must clearly explain the SAA-C03 exam connection, what wording in an exam question should make the learner think of SNS, what problem SNS solves, when SNS is the best answer and when SQS, EventBridge, Kinesis or another service is more suitable. Arrange all labs in a logical beginner learning order starting with IAM and SNS fundamentals, then subscriptions and publishing, fan-out, filtering, SQS integration, Lambda integration, monitoring, security, encryption, FIFO, failure handling, cross-account designs and finally full SAA-C03 architecture scenarios and troubleshooting labs. Follow the existing Study Tracker lab structure exactly and implement every lab as complete usable content. Do not include wording such as "Catalogue scope", "Instructions will be added later", "Defer detailed instructions", "Placeholder", "to be completed", "future lab", "coming later" or similar. Do not create empty Console actions or empty CLI actions. Every lab must contain real Console instructions, real CLI commands, verification, expected results, IAM requirements, explanations and cleanup actions.
